0.$description: The reduced-motion target. Not a speed — a destination. build.js appends a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that re-points the tier-2 transition and enter/exit tokens here, so honouring the preference costs one override instead of 73 hand-edited declarations. Loading loops (`--animation-spin`, `--animation-indeterminate`) are deliberately exempt.

75.$description: Barely perceptible. Colour-only flips on small controls.

150.$description: The workhorse — 103 of the hardcoded durations in components were this value.

linear.$description: Constant rate. Correct ONLY for continuous loops — spinners, indeterminate bars — where any acceleration reads as a stutter. Never for a state change.

standard.$description: The default curve, for a change that both starts and ends on screen — hover, colour, size. This is CSS's `ease`, which is what every transition in the system already used; it is kept verbatim so introducing this scale changes no rendered timing. Upgrading it to a designed cubic-bezier is a separate decision about how the system FEELS, batched with the contrast pass rather than smuggled into a restructure.

enter.$description: Decelerate. Things arriving on screen move fast then settle — menus, tooltips, toasts. Already the most-used curve in the system's keyframes (8 uses) with no token to point at, which is why they were all hardcoded.

exit.$description: Accelerate. Things leaving start slow and speed up out of frame. Pairs with `enter`; using `enter` on the way out is the most common motion tell.

emphasized.$description: Ease both ends. For a move that travels a real distance and stays on screen — drawers, sheets, indeterminate sweeps.
